bib.title: AI Agents Need Memory Control Over More Context

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AI Agents Need Memory Control Over More Context", Fouad Bousetouane (University of Chicago), arXiv 2601.11653v1 [q-bio.NC], 15 Jan 2026. It is a preprint with no venue.

COVERAGE: I read all 55,074 characters, including the references. The text of pages 1–2 and the table of contents came through partly; I read everything from the introduction on. The results exist only as figures (Figs 5–7), which the extraction does not read. I did not run the figure script.

**FIT WARNING.** This is a method paper with a live experiment, not a position paper. It fits only part of your target.
- It is about within-session, multi-turn state control: a bounded working state versus transcript replay versus RAG.
- It is not about learning from experience across tasks or sessions. There is no raw versus distilled lessons comparison, and no no-memory baseline.
- It reports no cost beyond memory tokens. There is no dollar, latency or compressor-call cost.
- **The text of the paper contains no numeric results.** The results section has only qualitative statements and figures. The only numbers in the text are setup counts, so the headline claims cannot be quoted with effect sizes.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Replacing transcript replay with one bounded, schema-governed state (the Compressed Cognitive State, CCS, rewritten each turn) keeps memory size flat and beats replay and RAG on hallucination and drift.
   - number: none. The text gives no effect sizes.
   - setup: three agents (replay, retrieval, ACC), 50-turn live episodes, IT ops, cybersecurity and healthcare. The model, judge model and compressor model are not named in the text.
   - quote: "The ACC agent stays near zero with rare small spikes, demonstrating stronger constraint retention and more stable goal sustaining over the full 50-turn horizon"
   - where: §5.5.4, around char 43000.
2. Transcript replay grows near-linearly in tokens. Retrieval and ACC stay bounded.
   - number: none. Only a qualitative plot (Fig 5).
   - setup: per-turn memory tokens across domains. Retrieval is restricted to the top-k artifacts per turn.
   - quote: "The baseline agent exhibits near-linear growth in context size over turns"
   - where: §5.5.1.
3. Hallucination rises with turn count for replay and RAG, with spikes after stress turns. ACC stays near zero.
   - number: none.
   - setup: claim audit against a judge-maintained canonical memory, H = U / max(1, S+U).
   - quote: "hallucination increases with turn count for the baseline and retrieval agents, with recurrent spikes after stress turns"
   - where: §5.5.3.
4. Outcome quality is only partly better. ACC is best on relevance and coherence and "competitive" on answer quality and instruction following.
   - number: none.
   - setup: judge scores 0–10, mean ± std over turns, blinded and order-randomised.
   - quote: "the ACC agent achieves the strongest relevance and coherence, while remaining competitive on answer quality and instruction following"
   - where: §5.5.2.
5. RAG memory needed its top-k cut to limit drift. This is a tuning disclosure that also shows how fragile the RAG baseline is.
   - number: top 5 in §5.5.1, top 3 in the Fig 5 caption and the conclusion. The paper contradicts itself.
   - quote: "we explicitly restrict recall to the top 5 artifacts per turn to limit drift escalation observed with larger retrieval sets"
   - where: §5.5.1.
6. Scale of the experiment.
   - number: 600 evaluations × 50 turns = 30,000 turns.
   - quote: "We launched 600 live evaluations for a total of 30,000 turns across all data."
   - where: §5.4.
7. Design claim: a schema-constrained write path, with recall separated from commitment, limits memory poisoning.
   - number: none. The CCS has 9 typed fields (episodic trace, semantic gist, focal entities, relational map, goal, constraints, predictive cue, uncertainty, artifact refs).
   - quote: "Retrieved artifacts are treated as external evidence and cannot directly modify the cognitive state unless explicitly incorporated by the CCM under the CCS schema constraint."
   - where: §3.1.

BASELINES AND TOKEN MATCHING
- **Baseline agent:** full transcript replay. It is the only full-context arm.
- **Retrieval agent:** its own isolated store, top-3 or top-5 artifacts per turn.
- **No-memory baseline:** none.
- **Tokens are not matched.** Replay grows without bound by design, and ACC is bounded by design. There is no matched-budget comparison, such as replay truncated to the CCS size or a sliding window.
- **Cost is not counted.** The extra per-turn CCM compressor call, and its tokens, latency and dollars, are not measured. The paper only recommends a small fine-tuned compressor to cut cost.
- **No ablations.** There is no ACC without the qualification gate, no ACC without the schema, and no plain-summary baseline.

LIMITS
- Judge-based evaluation only. The authors concede future work on "targeted human audits".
- The judge's canonical memory is built from user queries, and the same judge scores all answers.
- Agents run in a fixed order (baseline, retrieval, ACC). Judge identity and model details are missing.
- No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The authors state no limitations section.
- Domain inconsistency: finance appears in §5.1 and the conclusion, but the abstract and §5.4 list three domains and Fig 7 shows only three.
- The headline results are qualitative, and the "substantially lower" wording is not quantified in text.
- The paper handles no cross-session learning and no experience distillation. Its scope is working state.
- Many of the 41 references are unverifiable stubs. The reference list has duplicates (Cowan appears twice; Zheng appears twice) and the author self-cites a Kindle book.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Transcript replay and lost-in-the-middle: Liu et al., TACL 2024.
- RAG: Lewis et al., 2020 (arXiv); DPR: Karpukhin et al., EMNLP 2020.
- Self-RAG: Asai et al., 2023.
- MemGPT: Packer et al., 2023.
- Reflexion: Shinn et al., 2023.
- ReAct: Yao et al., 2022.
- Generative Agents: Park et al., 2023.
- LLM-as-judge: Zheng et al., 2023 (MT-Bench); G-Eval: Liu et al., 2023; Dubois et al., 2024 (length-controlled AlpacaEval).
- Cognitive science: Baddeley and Hitch 1974; Baddeley 2000 (episodic buffer); Cowan 2001; McClelland et al. 1995 (Complementary Learning Systems); Nagy et al. 2020 (optimal forgetting).

CODE
- None. The drift and hallucination metric definitions are worth keeping:
  - H_t = U_t / max(1, S_t+U_t)
  - D_t = (V_t+O_t) / max(1, |K_t|), with t=1 excluded.
  - Where: §5.3.
- Algorithm 1 (§3.3) is a per-turn loop: recall, qualify, commit and replace the CCS, act, then store the turn into the artifact store.

FIGURES
- **Fig 5 (p.25):** per-turn memory tokens across domains, and average memory by domain and agent. Replay grows with turn count while retrieval and ACC stay bounded. It is the one figure candidate, because it shows unbounded versus bounded memory faster than prose. Caveat: the caption says "top-3" while the text says "top-5".
- Fig 7 (hallucination and drift per turn) is the evidence for the main claim. I did not extract it or read its values.

PROBLEMS
- Figures were not extracted, so no numeric values from Figs 5–7 are available. All three need visual inspection before anything is cited from them.
- There were no embedded instructions in the text.
- The extraction garbled some formulas and the table of contents, though the content is recoverable.
